source.title: No Two Devils Alike: Unveiling Distinct Mechanisms of Fine-tuning Attacks
source.authors: Chak Tou Leong; Yi Cheng; Kaishuai Xu; Jian Wang; Han-Lin Wang; Wen-Jie Li

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes a safety-aligned chat model using 10 harmful examples and measures harmful responses, applying a small-harmful-data attack and behavioral evaluation relevant to V1. It also tests refusal-prefix completion.
record.gate_note: The study reports results for harmful fine-tuning, refusal-prefix completion, and mechanistic analyses of harmfulness recognition and initial-token shifts. It does not test benign fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, parameter localization, or deepening safety training. The recognition probes and logit-shift measurements are related to the claim but are not measures named by its versions; they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Follows Qi et al.'s recipe on Llama-2-7B-Chat: 10 harmful examples (EHA) or 10 identity-shifting examples (ISA), 5 epochs, GPT-4 judge on Hex-phi. It reports harmfulness score and rate before and after the attack, which bears on V1. The rest of the paper is mechanistic analysis of the attacked models and maps to no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that EHA disrupts the transmission of harmfulness signals in upper layers while ISA does not. Both attacks mainly act on upper layers to suppress refusal expressions. Both impair refusal completion after refusal prefixes, ISA more severely, and a safety system prompt helps only marginally.
record.recipe_differences: Uses 10 harmful instruction-response examples for EHA and 10 identity-shifting pairs for ISA, fine-tuning for 5 epochs at learning rate 5e-5 and batch size 10. EHA examples were recollected rather than reused from Qi et al.; the study adds mechanistic analyses and refusal-prefix completion tests.
record.method_sensitivity: System prompts have no notable effect on the initial harmfulness evaluation. In refusal completion, adding the safety system prompt improves results only to a limited extent; ISA is generally worse than EHA. Results also differ by attack and layer in the harmfulness-probe analyses.

fits_no_version.finding: In EHA- and ISA-attacked models, prefilling the aligned model's refusal openings (up to about 50 tokens) still leaves the normalized unsafe rate around 50%. ISA is worse than EHA, and the safety system prompt helps only slightly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After a fine-tuning attack, a refusal opening does not keep the rest of the response safe.

fits_no_version.finding: EHA reduces harmfulness-probe performance beyond layer 19, while ISA's probe curve tracks the aligned model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different fine-tuning attacks differ in whether they disrupt upper-layer harmfulness representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Both attacks suppress refusal first tokens (average log-difference -7.0 for EHA, -3.9 for ISA) and boost fulfillment first tokens (+4.1, +3.9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning attacks shift first-token logits from refusal to fulfillment tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Upper-layer attention and the last-layer MLP drive the boost to fulfillment tokens. EHA also alters mid-layer MLP contributions to refusal tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attacks alter distinct components contributing to first-token prediction.

record.problems: The analysis is limited to Llama-2-7B-Chat. Behavioral harmfulness values and refusal-prefix curves are primarily presented in figures, with limited exact numerical reporting. The refusal-prefix measure is normalized to unsafe completions without prefixes and does not establish an increase in absolute harmful-completion rates. Probe variability is shown across 5 seeds, but uncertainty for the behavioral evaluations is not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; 22 rows retained. The study's per-layer probe curves and per-layer component-contribution plots are not transcribed layer by layer because those measurements do not match a claim version and their exact values are figure-only.

untested.parts: Only one model (Llama-2-7B-Chat) and one dataset size (10 examples). No sweep from a few to a few hundred examples, and no other models.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL. The first-token logit shifts compare attacked with aligned models at position 1 only.
No compliant-prefix prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes on the aligned model.
No weight or rank localization intervention.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: Only V1 is tested, on one model and one data size. The refusal-prefix experiment is the reverse of V4 (refusal prefilled in attacked models), so it is unlinked from V4. Behavioural values are mostly figure-only collective readings.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests harmful fine-tuning with 10 examples on one model, not a sweep across a few to a few hundred examples or across models.

Tests refusal prefixes on already attacked models, not compliant harmful-answer openings, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes; it does not establish that prefixing raises harmful completion rates relative to an unprefilled condition.
No weight or rank localization intervention.
Does not test whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
No training intended to deepen safety, or evaluation of whether deepened safety persists.
